segments.title: Memory Palace
segments.content:
While listening to Ying Chanxi explain the problems to him, Li Luo explored the shape of these memories in his mind.

After about ten minutes, he finally had some understanding of his current situation.

Simply put, it was similar to hyperthymesia, but without too many side effects.

The entire 35 years of memories from before his rebirth were like recordings on videotapes. As long as he actively tried to recall them, he could instantly and accurately remember the scenes from that time.

He could even clearly recall "The Peach Blossom Spring," which he had only read a few times, without missing a single word.

If a normal person's memory was like a river, where trying to trace the past meant struggling upstream against the current, and past memories were already murky and unclear.

Then Li Luo's brain at this moment was like a vast memory palace.

All 35 years of his memories were neatly sealed within it, ready to be retrieved whenever Li Luo needed them.

But this ability of his was more like an active skill. When he wasn't actively thinking about things, he wouldn't face the problem of an overloaded brain from too many memories, unlike patients with hyperthymesia.

So, while Ying Chanxi was away in the bathroom, Li Luo hurriedly got up from his seat, and from a nearby bookshelf, took down a thick Xinhua Dictionary.

He then casually flipped to a random page and read a section of its contents, word by word.

Normally, after reading something like this once, an ordinary person would only remember a rough impression.

But Li Luo just had to recall it briefly, and all the content he had just read appeared in his mind, word for word.

He could remember it anytime he wanted.

"What are you doing?" Ying Chanxi asked when she came back to the bedroom from the bathroom and saw Li Luo holding a Xinhua Dictionary.

"Oh, just looking up a pinyin," Li Luo casually brushed it off, putting the Xinhua Dictionary back on the shelf, his heart already surging with excitement.

Because...

He tried to recall the exams he had experienced during the high school entrance exam in his past life—

Chinese—First question, which of the following options has the correct pinyin annotation for all the underlined characters?

Math—First question, 3a • (﹣2a)² = ?

It really worked!

As Li Luo recalled these test papers materializing in his mind, his lips and throat felt a little dry, and his heart pounded violently.

With these original questions, forget just meeting the cutoff score for a regular high school, Li Luo might even be able to take a shot at Yuhang Fuyi High School!

But when Li Luo finished recalling the math paper and tried to continue with the political history, science, and English papers, his head suddenly felt dizzy and swollen. He stopped immediately in fright, frowning and clutching his head.

Ugh...

Li Luo frowned at the problem Ying Chanxi had told him to think about, pretending to be solving it seriously while actually trying to relieve the throbbing pain in his head.

He then realized that his memory palace's recall ability was not completely without side effects.

Every recall must consume his mental power and energy. Trying to recall more content in a short period could easily damage his brain.

This consumption was especially exacerbated by more detailed content, like the specific questions on an exam paper.

But even so, for Li Luo, the remaining time should be enough for him to recall the rest of the exam papers.

The good news was that once recalled, these papers seemed to be truly imprinted in his brain. Retrieving them no longer consumed mental energy and he could flip through them at will.

The only unfortunate thing was that Li Luo had never checked the answers to the entrance exam in his past life, so the correct answers were naturally not saved in his memory palace.

He only remembered that his score on the entrance exam in his past life was only 417, ranking him 4897th in the district.

The cutoff score for regular high school that year was 420.

And the cutoff for Yuhang Fuyi High School was a staggering 512.

Yuhang Fuyi High School, located in the relatively remote Yinjiang District of Yuhang City, probably ranks among the top five in the entire city for its teaching staff and academic results.

Every year, there were about seven to eight thousand students taking the entrance exam in the entire Yinjiang District, but Yuhang Fuyi High School would only enroll about 640 new students.

Among them, 160 had already been admitted through independent recruitment, leaving only about 480 spots for the students taking the main entrance exam.

Excluding the top students who would transfer to the key high schools in the city center, to get into the affiliated high school, one had to rank at least in the top six hundred in the district to even have a chance.

Ranking in the top five hundred was considered a safe bet.

This level of difficulty, whether for the 15-year-old Li Luo or the 35-year-old Li Luo, was hell-level.

Normally, he wouldn't even have to think about it.

But at this moment, after discovering the entrance exam papers sealed deep within his memory, Li Luo suddenly felt like he still had a chance.

"What are you spacing out for?" Ying Chanxi looked strangely at the dazed Li Luo, slightly displeased. "Don't get distracted, did you figure out this problem?"

"Um... can you explain it one more time?" Li Luo came back to his senses and said with a thick-skinned face.

He made a quick comparison and found that the problem Ying Chanxi was explaining was the same type as the fifth multiple-choice question on the math entrance exam.

If he could solve this problem, he could solve that multiple-choice question on the exam.

Thinking this, Li Luo's spirits lifted.

He couldn't possibly write down the questions from the math entrance exam in front of Ying Chanxi and ask her to teach him.

That would be too suspicious. If Ying Chanxi saw the math questions after the exam, it would pose a potential risk.

But as long as he could understand the similar math problem types, and then follow Ying Chanxi's line of thought to solve the math exam in his head, wouldn't he be able to get these math problems done in advance?

For subjects like Chinese, with questions like reading comprehension, it would be almost impossible to get a perfect score without the standard answer to copy from.

But for a subject like math, as long as he found the corresponding problem type and understood the solution method, Li Luo could calculate the answers in advance.

Even for the open-ended questions, as long as he had the problem-solving thought process and steps for a similar type, he could solve it to about eighty or ninety percent accuracy.

After confirming this, Li Luo's passion for studying was completely ignited.

Ying Chanxi could clearly feel that Li Luo had suddenly become several times more serious. He even proactively picked out some problems and asked her to explain them a few more times.

This made her feel somewhat gratified, and she also perked up, carefully breaking down and explaining the solutions to him.

...

Around five o'clock in the evening, the sound of a key turning in the lock came from the front door.

Soon, the shuffling sounds of changing shoes and low whispers came from outside.

Probably having seen the shoes at the entrance, Li Luo's mother, Lin Xiuhong, walked to the bedroom door, knocked, and asked, "Li Luo, is Xixi here?"

"I'm here, Auntie." Ying Chanxi was closer to the door. She stood up, opened it, and poked her head out to speak to Lin Xiuhong outside. "Auntie Lin~ I'm helping Li Luo review for his exams tomorrow."

Upon hearing this, Lin Xiuhong was first taken aback. Then, peeking through the crack of the door, she was a little surprised to see Li Luo hunched over his desk, studying seriously.

Immediately, she smiled happily, nodding repeatedly. "Good, good, thank you for your hard work, Xixi. Your uncle and I bought a lot of groceries. Why don't you have dinner with us today?"

"Mhm." Ying Chanxi nodded in agreement, a sweet smile on her face. "I've been craving your cooking, Auntie Lin."

"Hehe, they're all your favorites. Coke chicken wings, scrambled eggs with tomato, eggplant with minced pork..." Lin Xiuhong listed off a series of dishes.

The more Ying Chanxi heard, the brighter her eyes became. "Auntie Lin, do you need help? I can be your assistant."

"No, no, your uncle is back too, we'll cook." Lin Xiuhong waved her hands repeatedly. "You should help that boy Li Luo review some more. Every extra day of study is a good thing."

"Okay, I will."

After they finished talking.

The bedroom door was closed again.

And just as Ying Chanxi closed the door and turned to sit back down, Li Luo's shoulders, which had been trembling slightly, also calmed down.

But if one paid close attention, one could still see that the grip Li Luo had on his pen was much tighter than before.

"Phew..." Li Luo let out a long breath, suppressing the turbulent emotions within him, barely managing to keep his composure in front of Ying Chanxi.

Just now, when he heard his mother's familiar voice, an image of his mother twenty years later instantly flashed through Li Luo's mind: lying on a hospital bed, her lips pale, her face sallow and gaunt, covered in wrinkles.

And now, Lin Xiuhong was twenty years younger... Li Luo was afraid that the moment he saw her, he wouldn't be able to stop himself from crying out loud.

So he forcibly resisted the impulse in his heart and didn't turn his head for even a glance.

Beside him, Ying Chanxi didn't notice Li Luo's strangeness and continued to teach him problems.

And in the kitchen, Lin Xiuhong was also chatting with her husband.

"If that boy Li Luo was half as well-behaved as Xixi, his grades wouldn't be this bad."

"Boys mature late, that's all." Li Guohong handed over the vegetables he had just washed and comforted her. "He'll get better once he's in high school."

"We don't even know if he can get into a regular high school yet," Lin Xiuhong said, worried. "At the midterm parent-teacher conference, his teacher told me that Li Luo's current grades are very precarious. If he's off by even a few points, he'll have to go to a vocational high school."

Li Guohong was silent for a moment, then said, "Remember my cousin?"

"What about him?" Lin Xiuhong was slightly puzzled.

"His wife's brother-in-law is the dean of students at No. 13 High School," Li Guohong said. "I mentioned Li Luo's situation to him before. He said No. 13 High has spots for out-of-district students every year. If he's short a few points on the exam, we can pay a selection fee and still get Li Luo into a regular high school."

"Really?" Lin Xiuhong's face lit up, feeling a bit more secure, but then she asked, "How much is the selection fee?"

"A one-time fee of 30,000, and then the annual tuition is two thousand more than for regular students."

"That expensive?" Lin Xiuhong subconsciously frowned, but then she sighed. "If that boy really doesn't pull himself together, we'll just have to spend the money."

"Alright, don't think like that." Li Guohong patted his wife's shoulder comfortingly. "Look, isn't Ying Chanxi helping him study? The top student in the grade tutoring your son, he should have no problem with the regular high school cutoff."

"What's the use of that?" Lin Xiuhong pursed her lips. "If it were that useful, what was he doing before? It's the last day, and only now does he think to ask Xixi for tutoring?"

"A last-minute prayer is better than no prayer at all," was all Li Guohong could say. "The exam is tomorrow. Let's not say anything upsetting in front of the kid later."

"Do you need to tell me that? I know what to do."

Lin Xiuhong sliced a plate of apples and handed the kitchen knife to Li Guohong. "I'll take a plate of fruit in, you cut the vegetables."

After speaking, Lin Xiuhong stuck two toothpicks into the apple slices, carried the plate out of the kitchen, went to her son's bedroom door, and knocked gently.

"Auntie Lin, what's up?" Ying Chanxi opened the door, poked her head out, and saw the plate of fruit in Lin Xiuhong's hand.

"Here, dinner will be a while. Have some fruit first." Lin Xiuhong handed the plate over and glanced at Li Luo inside the room.

At that moment, Li Luo had just finished listening to Ying Chanxi explain a major math problem. He was trying to figure out how to solve a similar geometry problem from the entrance exam paper, concentrating intently on his calculations.

Seeing her son looking so serious, Lin Xiuhong felt a little relieved. "You two carry on, I won't disturb you."

"Okay, Auntie Lin," Ying Chanxi responded sweetly and carried the plate back to her seat.

Seeing that Li Luo was still focused on the problems on the paper, Ying Chanxi proactively picked up a toothpick, speared a slice of apple, and held it to his lips.

Feeling something by his mouth, Li Luo looked down and came back to his senses.

He then looked at Ying Chanxi with some astonishment, blinking his eyes, his gaze a little dazed.

"What are you looking at?" Ying Chanxi wiggled the toothpick in her hand. "Seeing as you're studying so seriously, this is a special treat, just for today."

"Ying Chanxi."

"Hm?"

"You don't have a crush on me, do you?"

"...I'd have a crush on a blockhead like you!" Ying Chanxi's brows shot up, and she was about to pull the toothpick back. "Fine, don't eat it."

"Hey, don't!" Li Luo quickly reached out and pressed down on Ying Chanxi's small hand, then leaned his head forward and snatched the apple slice into his mouth.

Ying Chanxi rolled her eyes at him, stuck the toothpick back into another slice, then picked up the other one and speared a piece for herself.

Feeling the pure and joyful friendship with his childhood friend once more, Li Luo's mood was exceptionally bright. Savoring the sweetness of the apple in his mouth, he buried his head and continued to tackle the difficult problems.

"Here, have another piece."

An apple slice was held to Li Luo's lips.

Li Luo subconsciously opened his mouth, only to bite on air, his teeth clinking together.

"Haha!" Seeing him fall for it, Ying Chanxi laughed triumphantly.

But in the next second, Li Luo had already raised an eyebrow, snatched the toothpick from her hand, and stuffed the apple slice on it into his mouth.

"Hey!" Seeing this, Ying Chanxi's face flushed with urgency. "What are you doing! That's my toothpick!"

"Oh? No wonder it didn't taste as good as the last one."

"...You're asking for it!"

A side of her personality she had never shown to her schoolmates blossomed without reservation in the boy's bedroom.
